newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Nkomati JV nickel output at 3,000 T/month.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Nkomati JV nickel output at 3,000 T/month.

text.p: South Africa's Nkomati MSB joint venture has reached full production at its high grade plant and output has reached 3,000 tonnes of nickel concentrate a month, a spokesman for Avmin Ltd said on Thursday.
The Nkomati project is a joint venture between Avmin (75 percent) and Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd (25 percent).
Avmin technical director Jerry Robbertse told Reuters the operation to exploit a small high-grade portion of the Massive Sulphide Body (MSB) was running at full output.
"It is in full production at the moment", Robbertse said.
The high grade operation came into production in January 1997.
"It is producing at the rate of some 3,000 tonnes of nickel (concentrate) at the moment and work is going on, looking at the possible expansions and extensions of that," Robbertse said.
Avmin said output was around 10,000 tonnes a month which resulted in some 3,000 tonnes of nickel in concentrate a month.
The venture aims to mine nickel and copper, cobalt and platinum group metals as byproducts of nickel.
Avmin said earlier this year it had completed a feasibility study into the main Nkomati nickel mine.
The study had progressed satisfactorily and was currently undergoing final checks before being presented to the various stakeholders.

The MSB consists of an in-situ geological resource of three million tonnes, grading 2.04 percent nickel, 1.13 percent copper, 0.09 percent cobalt and 6.17 grammes per tonne combined platinum, palladium, rhodium and gold.
